subject.title: memory_search: transient sync timeout masks as persistent provider failure / "database is not open"

question: When a valid memory index exists but post-restart dirty synchronization is slow, should interactive `memory_search` serve that index and schedule sync separately, or remain freshness-blocking with improved phase-specific errors?
rationale: The error-reporting and cancellation boundary may be a narrow defect, but returning stale results changes freshness semantics and should not be selected by automated repair.

options.title: Separate interactive search from dirty sync
options.body: Return results from a valid current index, queue or continue dirty synchronization outside the interactive deadline, and make result freshness explicit.

options.title: Keep freshness-blocking search
options.body: Retain blocking synchronization but add phase attribution, cancellation-safe manager ownership, and a user-facing recovery path for slow sync.

options.title: Collect timing evidence first
options.body: Add scoped diagnostics before choosing either behavior if current-main traces cannot distinguish provider initialization from indexing work.

recommendation.title: Separate interactive search from dirty sync
recommendation.body: Return results from a valid current index, queue or continue dirty synchronization outside the interactive deadline, and make result freshness explicit.
